session.title: Rights, Minorities and the Advisory Committee

primarySource.publisher: Parliament Digital Library, Lok Sabha Secretariat

transcriptReference.publisher: Constitution of India / Centre for Law and Policy Research
transcriptReference.note: Used for paragraph-level navigation and speaker segmentation; Parliament Digital Library remains canonical.

speakers.name: Dr. Rajendra Prasad
speakers.positionSummary: Returns the House from budget Committee to plenary, manages amendments to the Advisory Committee motion, rules on election procedure, puts the amended resolution to vote and later closes the budget.

speakers.name: Satyanarayan Sinha
speakers.positionSummary: Moves the House back into open plenary session, moves the Vice-President election resolution and later moves closure of the Advisory Committee debate.

speakers.name: Govind Ballabh Pant
speakers.positionSummary: Moves the Advisory Committee on rights, minorities and tribal/excluded areas, explains its representation structure and accepts the amendments incorporated into the final resolution.

speakers.name: Sardar Harnam Singh
speakers.positionSummary: Seconds Pant and argues that minority protection must cover religious, cultural, economic, administrative and political dimensions.

speakers.name: Damber Singh Gurung
speakers.positionSummary: First questions whether members had adequate notice and later argues that Gorkhas require representation in the body charged with minority and backward-area safeguards.

speakers.name: K. M. Munshi
speakers.positionSummary: Moves the amendments that restructure the Advisory Committee, names the initial membership, expands presidential nominations, sets report deadlines and changes vacancy procedure.

speakers.name: J. J. M. Nichols-Roy
speakers.positionSummary: Withdraws proposed amendments but later supports sub-committee co-option as a route for diverse tribal areas while asking consideration for additional Christian representation.

speakers.name: K. Santhanam
speakers.positionSummary: Declines an earlier amendment, later warns the Advisory Committee not to absorb functions of the whole Assembly and urges early circulation of its reports.

speakers.name: Syamanandan Sahaya
speakers.positionSummary: Challenges the named-member method as a departure from proportional representation and later raises a point of order about future committee elections.

speakers.name: Jaipal Singh
speakers.positionSummary: Challenges the adequacy and distribution of tribal representation, points to omitted tribal groups and women, and treats the Committee as a test of the Assembly's treatment of Adivasis.

speakers.name: Kiron Sankar Roy
speakers.positionSummary: Interjects during Jaipal Singh's historical argument.

speakers.name: Frank Anthony
speakers.positionSummary: Rejects the claim that Anglo-Indians are over-represented and argues that the Cabinet Mission intended smaller minorities to influence minority safeguards.

speakers.name: N. Gopalaswami Ayyangar
speakers.positionSummary: Points out the mandatory need for a quorum and moves a one-third quorum for the Advisory Committee and its sub-committees.

speakers.name: Dakshayani Velayudhan
speakers.stance: Scheduled Caste voice beyond sectional label
speakers.positionSummary: Argues that Scheduled Caste members should not be treated as speaking only for Scheduled Castes and presses for representation among Hindus from Muslim-majority provinces.

speakers.name: Lakshminarayan Sahu
speakers.positionSummary: Argues that Orissa and its excluded/partially excluded areas are neglected in the proposed membership.

speakers.name: Jairamdas Daulatram
speakers.positionSummary: Urges the House not to narrow the Committee's scope and asks it to reconcile minority requirements with wider national sentiment.

speakers.name: S. Nagappa
speakers.positionSummary: Questions the distribution of seats among communities and asks the Committee to protect groups whose numerical representation is weak.

speakers.name: B. Das
speakers.positionSummary: Warns that safeguards designed at an all-India level may impose disproportionate administrative and financial burdens on poorer provinces such as Orissa.

speakers.name: R. K. Sidhwa
speakers.positionSummary: Requests to speak after closure is moved but the House proceeds to the closure vote.

speakers.name: J. B. Kripalani
speakers.positionSummary: Seconds the amendment that substitutes a named initial membership for the original proportional-representation election mechanism.

speakers.name: N. V. Gadgil
speakers.positionSummary: After the in-camera Committee discussion concludes, formally moves the budget resolution in plenary.

speakers.name: Deshbandhu Gupta
speakers.positionSummary: Asks whether government service rules apply to Constituent Assembly staff, prompting the Chair to assert the Assembly's separate administrative authority.

speakers.name: Unidentified Member
speakers.positionSummary: The transcript contains short interventions without a named speaker, including an Orissa/Andhra interjection and the formal seconding of the budget resolution.

interventions.summary: The President proposes temporarily leaving the budget Committee to dispose of plenary resolutions, and the House formally returns to open session.
Satyanarayan Sinha moves that the Assembly proceed to elect a Vice-President and explains why a standing presiding substitute is needed when the President is absent.
Pant seconds the Vice-President election motion.
The motion is adopted; the President sets the nomination deadline and the procedure if a poll becomes necessary.

Pant moves the Advisory Committee on fundamental rights, minorities, tribal and excluded areas. He argues that further delay for absent League members is no longer justified, explains the proposed representation of communities and tribal areas, and connects the Committee to guarantees already accepted in the Objectives Resolution.
The Chair calls Sardar Harnam Singh to second the resolution.
Harnam Singh seconds the motion and frames minority protection as a multi-dimensional constitutional problem requiring a settlement acceptable to affected communities.
The President decides to take proposed amendments clause by clause.
Damber Singh Gurung questions whether members had sufficient notice of the resolution. The Chair distinguishes the already-circulated motion from amendments not yet moved.
Munshi moves to increase the maximum Advisory Committee size from 68 to 72; the House adopts the amendment.
Nichols-Roy declines to move his amendment at this stage.
Santhanam also declines to move his proposed amendment.

Munshi replaces the original election formula with a named initial membership. He reads the proposed members category by category—minority communities, Scheduled Castes, Sikhs, Christians, Anglo-Indians, Parsis, tribal and excluded areas, and general members.
Kripalani seconds Munshi's named-membership amendment.
Nichols-Roy says he had considered adding names but withdraws the proposal rather than disturb the agreed number.
Sahaya argues that replacing proportional representation with a predetermined list creates an unhealthy precedent and asks the House to preserve the election method stated in its Rules.
Jaipal Singh rejects any suggestion that tribal peoples seek foreign protection and insists they look to their own countrymen for a fair settlement.
Kiron Sankar Roy briefly challenges Jaipal Singh's historical timescale.

Jaipal Singh argues that representation cannot be judged only by the number of tribal seats. He identifies missing communities and the absence of a tribal woman, and asks whether independent India will treat Adivasis differently from the colonial system.
interventions.excerpt: This House is on trial; let us see what happens.

interventions.summary: Pant clarifies that there is one Advisory Committee capable of creating sub-committees rather than a separately constituted Fundamental Rights Committee; the exchange closes without Jaipal Singh seeking additional seats.

Munshi removes a redundant election provision, raises presidential nomination capacity to accommodate Muslim representatives if the League joins, fixes report deadlines for fundamental and minority rights, and allows the President to fill casual vacancies while the Assembly is adjourned.
Gopalaswami Ayyangar points to the Rules' mandatory quorum requirement and moves a one-third quorum for the Committee and its sub-committees.

Frank Anthony rejects the suggestion that Anglo-Indians are over-represented and argues that the Cabinet Mission specifically intended smaller minorities to have enough presence to influence safeguards affecting them.

Gurung argues that no Gorkha appears on the proposed Committee even though Gorkhas are a distinct, backward community with a strong presence in a partially excluded area. He asks how their interests will reach the body charged with safeguards.
Santhanam warns the Committee against expanding into questions reserved for the whole Assembly or Sections and urges reports to be circulated well before debate so members can prepare.
Sahaya argues that the amended motion leaves future election procedure unclear. Munshi relies on Rule 46's exception, and the President rules the amendment in order.
Dakshayani Velayudhan argues that Scheduled Caste members should not be confined to representing only a sectional category; they also have a claim to represent Hindus in Muslim-majority provinces.
Lakshminarayan Sahu argues that Orissa and its extensive excluded and partially excluded areas have been neglected and again favours a transparent election method.
Jairamdas Daulatram asks the House not to restrict the Committee's future work in advance and urges reconciliation between minority needs and national sentiment.

Nagappa questions why some communities receive what he sees as disproportionate representation and asks Committee members to protect less adequately represented Scheduled Caste interests rather than behave as sectional delegates.

Nichols-Roy says the diversity of tribal areas cannot be captured by a single list but sees sub-committee co-option as a practical route. He also asks the President to consider additional Indian Christian representation from Orissa.
An unidentified member asks about Andhra during the representation discussion.

B. Das argues that minority safeguards must not obscure independence or ignore provincial economic capacity. He presses Orissa's claim to representation and warns against imposing uniform financial burdens on poorer provinces.
Satyanarayan Sinha moves that the question be put.
Sidhwa asks to say a few words, but the Chair notes that closure has been moved and the House adopts closure.

Pant accepts Munshi's amendments and later Ayyangar's quorum amendment. He defends the membership method as group-based selection endorsed by the whole Assembly, acknowledges inevitable omissions and argues that calibre, accommodation and consensus matter more than exact numerical proportionality.

The President reads the amended structure into the record, including a maximum of 72 members, one-third quorum and deadlines for interim reports on fundamental and minority rights. The House adopts the resolution and adjourns for lunch before returning to budget Committee.
After the in-camera Committee discussion is concluded, Gadgil formally moves the budget resolution in plenary.
An unnamed voice seconds the budget resolution in the printed transcript.
The President puts the expenditure and member-allowance resolutions to the House. The budget is adopted and the day's listed business closes.

Deshbandhu Gupta asks whether government service rules apply to Assembly employees. Rajendra Prasad replies that the Assembly's own servants are not government servants and that the Assembly may make its own rules.
The President announces an open session for the next morning and adjourns the Assembly to 25 January.
